---
title: "Exploring Hennepin County Zip Codes: An Interactive Map"
author: "Khalid Shire"
date: "2026-10-18"
categories: [maps, hennepin, interactive]
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(zipcodeR)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

hennepin_zips <- search_county("Hennepin", "MN")

zips <- st_read(dsn = "../../../day11/shapefiles/Zip_Codes", layer = "Zip_Codes", quiet = TRUE)

zip_map <- zips |>
  left_join(hennepin_zips, by = c("NAME_TXT" = "zipcode")) |>
  mutate(label = paste0("Zip: ", NAME_TXT,
                        "<br>Median income: $", median_household_income))

p <- ggplot(zip_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = median_household_income, text = label)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lavender", high = "purple4", na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(
    title = "Median Household Income by Zip Code",
    fill = "Median income ($)"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## What this shows

This is an interactive version of my zip code map of Hennepin County. Hover over any zip code to see its number and median household income. Use the toolbar in the top right to zoom in and pan around, which helps with the small zip codes on the east side that are hard to see on a static map.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

## Search the data

The table below has the same numbers. You can sort any column by clicking its header, or type in the search box to find a zip code.

```{r}
#| echo: false

hennepin_zips |>
  filter(!is.na(median_household_income)) |>
  select(Zip = zipcode, City = major_city, Population = population,
         `Median income` = median_household_income,
         `Median home value` = median_home_value) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE)
```

## How to read it

- Darker purple means higher median household income.
- Grey zip codes have no data, mostly PO Box zip codes.
- A median describes the middle household in a zip code, so individual households can be much higher or lower.
